item.text:
**Assessment**
I found no solid 2024 evidence that Sisi personally incited hatred, revenge, dehumanization, or violence against opponents, minorities, migrants, journalists, or civil-society groups. The public record I found cuts the other way: his official Gaza statements repeatedly use humanitarian and ceasefire language. The main contrary material is sharp anti-Israel condemnation and domestic repression of critics, but neither is a clear example of personal hate incitement against protected groups.

**Claims**
- **President El-Sisi’s Speech at the Urgent Humanitarian Response for Gaza Conference** | Presidency of the Republic of Egypt | **Jun. 11, 2024** | https://sis.gov.eg/en/presidency/speeches-telegrams-posts/president-el-sisi-s-speech-at-the-urgent-humanitarian-response-for-gaza-conference/  
  Sisi described Palestinians in Gaza as innocent civilians, condemned starvation and siege, invoked international law, and called for protecting civilians and releasing hostages and detainees. This is strong evidence against personal dehumanization or incitement.  
  **QIDs:** 3B.3, 2B.6, 2B.7, 2B.10

- **Call for Action: Urgent Humanitarian Response for Gaza** | United Nations | **Jun. 11, 2024** | https://www.un.org/unispal/document/statement-by-co-chairs-urgent-humanitarian-response-for-gaza-11jun24/  
  The co-chair statement, which includes Sisi, centers civilian casualties, humanitarian access, and international law. It does not contain hate speech or calls for revenge; it reinforces a non-incendiary public posture.  
  **QIDs:** 3B.3, 2B.7, 2B.10

- **President El-Sisi: Egypt rejects liquidation of Palestinian cause, forced displacement of Palestinians** | SIS / Egypt Today / Bahrain News Agency | **May 17, 2024** | https://africa.sis.gov.eg/english/africa-today/african-news/president-el-sisi-egypt-rejects-liquidation-of-palestinian-cause-forced-displacement-of-palestinians/  
  Sisi condemned Israeli escalation and insisted on protecting Palestinians and rejecting forced displacement. This is accusatory and politically charged, but it is still not an incitement to violence or dehumanization of a protected group.  
  **QIDs:** 3B.3, 2B.6, 2B.7

- **Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis** | Amnesty International | **May 13, 2024** | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/  
  Amnesty documents arrests and repression of protesters, workers, and online critics. This shows hostility to dissent, but it is indirect evidence only: I did not find Sisi personally urging hate or violence against these groups.  
  **QIDs:** 3B.3, 3B.1, 3B.2, 2B.6

- **Egypt: More than 100 arbitrarily detained over calls for anti-government protests** | Amnesty International | **Jul. 18, 2024** | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/  
  Security forces detained protesters and dissenters over calls for demonstrations. Again, this supports a coercive political climate, but not direct personal incitement by Sisi against a social group.  
  **QIDs:** 3B.3, 3B.1, 3B.2, 2B.6

- **SIS responds to Israeli claims about its borders with Gaza** | State Information Service | **Jan. 23, 2024** | https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/press-releases/sis-egypt-responds-to-israeli-claims-about-its-borders-with-gaza/  
  Egypt denied smuggling allegations and stressed Sinai security efforts after 2013. This is defensive denial, not hate incitement; it does not establish any personal appeal to revenge or violence.  
  **QIDs:** 3B.3, 2B.5, 2B.9

**Search gap**
I did not find a credible 2024 speech, interview, or official post in which Sisi personally called for hatred, revenge, dehumanization, or violence against opponents, minorities, migrants, journalists, or civil society. The strongest negative evidence is repression of critics and harsh war rhetoric about Israel, but that still falls short of the specific incitement standard in 3B.3.
